title: Travis Kalanick’s robotics startup Atoms taps former Uber finance chief as CFO
excerpt: Kalanick continues to get the band back together, after acquiring Anthony Levandowski's autonomy startup, and even soliciting investment from Uber.
content_html:
Another former Uber executive is joining Travis Kalanick’s robotics and industrial AI startup Atoms, just a few weeks after it raised $1.7 billion.

Gautam Gupta, the former finance chief under Kalanick, said in social media posts on Wednesday that he has joined Atoms as chief financial officer. Gupta spent more than four years at Uber until he left in July 2017, just a few weeks after Kalanick resigned as CEO. (Gupta had announced his intention to leave that May.)

Hiring Gupta continues a trend of Kalanick getting the Uber band back together at Atoms. Earlier this year, Atoms acquired mining autonomy startup Pronto, which is run by former Uber (and former Google) self-driving engineer Anthony Levandowski. According to LinkedIn, a number of former top Uber employees who worked with Kalanick also work at Atoms, which was previously called CloudKitchens.

“On many levels, this round is a bit of unfinished business. Fuel to complete the bits-to-atoms story arc we started at Uber, continued at CloudKitchens, and will now finish at Atoms,” Kalanick wrote when he announced the $1.7 billion funding round last month.

Uber even joined the round as an investor, reuniting the company with the founder it pushed out in 2017 after a series of scandals and complaints of widespread sexual harassment and discrimination. Uber hasn’t disclosed how much it contributed. The Information reported $100 million, a figure that TechCrunch has also been able to confirm.

Kalanick has said he wants Atoms to work on mining, food, and transportation, though his posts to date about the startup have been less about specifics and more about wanting to “go up against the final boss, Nature and its fierce resistance to change.”

Gupta invested in Uber in 2012 when he was a vice president at Goldman Sachs, and then joined the company in 2013.

“[T]he single biggest reason I joined was — Travis. I believed he possessed a magical mix of genius and intensity that made me want to bet on the person, not the market,” Gupta wrote Wednesday. “First one in, last one out, every day. Breaking down walls of regulations, unions, city bureaucracies, etc. Had he not pioneered ridesharing, I don’t think anyone else had the fortitude to fight through one adversity after another to create a whole new market worth hundreds of billions out of nothing.”

Gupta wrote Wednesday that A*, the VC firm he co-founded in 2020 after three years at Opendoor, invested in Atoms in what was the “largest investment in the history of our fund.” Gupta is stepping down from A* to take on the CFO role at Atoms, according to his LinkedIn profile.

Sean O’Kane is a reporter who has spent a decade covering the rapidly-evolving business and technology of the transportation industry, including Tesla and the many startups chasing Elon Musk. Most recently, he was a reporter at Bloomberg News where he helped break stories about some of the most notorious EV SPAC flops. He previously worked at The Verge, where he also covered consumer technology, hosted many short- and long-form videos, performed product and editorial photography, and once nearly passed out in a Red Bull Air Race plane.

content_html_zh:
另一位前 Uber 高管即将加入 Travis Kalanick 的机器人和工业人工智能初创公司 Atoms，而就在几周前，Atoms 筹集了 17 亿美元资金。

卡兰尼克手下的前财务总监高塔姆·古普塔 (Gautam Gupta) 周三在社交媒体帖子中表示，他已加入 Atoms 担任首席财务官。 古普塔在 Uber 工作了四年多，直到 2017 年 7 月离开，也就是卡兰尼克辞去首席执行官职务几周后。 （古普塔在那年五月宣布他打算离开。）

聘请古普塔延续了卡兰尼克让 Uber 团队在 Atoms 重新团结起来的趋势。 今年早些时候，Atoms 收购了采矿自动化初创公司 Pronto，该公司由前 Uber（和前谷歌）自动驾驶工程师 Anthony Levandowski 运营。 据LinkedIn称，一些曾与卡兰尼克共事的Uber前高级员工也在Atoms工作，该公司以前被称为CloudKitchens。

“从很多层面上来说，这一轮都有点未完成的任务。 为完成我们从 Uber 开始、在 CloudKitchens 继续、现在将在 Atoms 完成的从比特到原子的故事线提供动力，”卡兰尼克上个月宣布这一轮 17 亿美元融资时写道。

Uber 甚至作为投资者加入了这轮融资，在一系列丑闻以及对广泛的性骚扰和歧视的投诉后，该公司与 2017 年被赶出的创始人重新合并。 Uber 尚未透露其贡献了多少。 The Information 报道称其营收为 1 亿美元，TechCrunch 也证实了这一数字。

卡兰尼克曾表示，他希望 Atoms 涉足采矿、食品和运输领域，尽管他迄今为止关于这家初创公司的帖子较少涉及具体细节，更多的是想要“对抗最终的老板，大自然及其对变革的强烈抵制”。

古普塔于 2012 年在高盛担任副总裁时投资了 Uber，并于 2013 年加入该公司。

“我加入的最大原因是——特拉维斯。 我相信他拥有天才和强度的神奇结合，这让我想把赌注押在他身上，而不是市场上，”古普塔周三写道。 “每天第一个进来，最后一个出去。 打破法规、工会、城市官僚机构等的围墙。如果不是他开创了拼车服务，我认为没有人有勇气克服一个又一个的逆境，从无到有地创造一个价值数千亿的全新市场。”

Gupta 周三写道，他在 Opendoor 工作三年后于 2020 年与他人共同创立的风险投资公司 A* 投资了 Atoms，这是“我们基金历史上最大的一笔投资”。 根据 Gupta 的 LinkedIn 个人资料，他将从 A* 辞职，转而担任 Atoms 的首席财务官。

肖恩·奥凯恩 (Sean O’Kane) 是一名记者，花了十年时间报道交通运输行业快速发展的业务和技术，包括特斯拉和许多追逐埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的初创公司。 最近，他担任彭博新闻社的记者，帮助报道了一些最臭名昭著的 EV SPAC 失败的故事。 他此前曾在 The Verge 工作，在那里他还报道过消费技术、主持过许多短视频和长视频、进行产品和社论摄影，并有一次在红牛空中竞赛飞机上差点昏倒。
